technical_and_design_decisions: Port existing Spring XD modules (Log, field-value-counter, aggregate-counter, gauge, rich-gauge) to Spring Cloud Stream repository as sink modules, adapting them to the new framework structure.
Integrate Amazon Kinesis as a sink using the existing Spring Cloud Stream Kinesis binder for seamless streaming pipeline support.
Implement job DSL leveraging Spring Batch framework to enable workflow creation and job orchestration, maintaining compatibility with Spring ecosystem.
Add Apache Flink as a processor in Spring Cloud Stream, incorporating support for streaming machine learning abstractions.
assumptions: The 's-c-s' repository refers to Spring Cloud Stream, a Spring project for building message-driven microservices.
XD refers to Spring XD, a data ingestion and batch processing framework, with modules being ported to align with Spring Cloud Stream.
The developer has access to source code repositories and is proficient in Java and Spring technologies.
Effort estimates assume a standard 8-hour workday and typical developer productivity for similar Spring-based projects.
Testing includes unit tests, integration tests, and basic system tests to ensure functionality across modules.
Documentation updates cover API references and user guides for new features and modules.
No major architectural changes are required, as the porting involves adapting existing code to the Spring Cloud Stream model.

activities.activity_description: Review all user stories, analyze existing codebase for XD modules and Spring Cloud Stream, design integration points, and create implementation plan for the software increment.

Port the Log, field-value-counter, aggregate-counter, gauge, and rich-gauge modules from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream repository, ensuring they function correctly as sink modules with minimal code changes.
Configure and integrate the Kinesis module as a sink in Spring Cloud Stream, leveraging the Kinesis binder to support streaming pipelines and validate with sample data flows.

Design and implement a job DSL using Spring Batch, allowing users to define comprehensive workflows and orchestrate jobs via a domain-specific language, including syntax design and integration testing.
Add support for using Apache Flink as a processor in Spring Cloud Stream, enabling streaming machine learning abstractions, and ensure compatibility with existing processor abstractions.
Perform unit testing for each module and feature, integration testing across the software increment, and system testing to verify end-to-end functionality in streaming pipelines.
Update project documentation to include new modules, job DSL usage, and Flink processor integration, and conduct code reviews to ensure code quality and adherence to standards.
